title: Maximum Subarray Min-Product
summary: Given an array of integers nums, find the maximum min-product of any non-empty contiguous subarray.
statement: Given an array of integers nums, find the maximum min-product of any non-empty contiguous subarray. The min-product is calculated as the minimum value in the subarray multiplied by the sum of the subarray elements. Return the result modulo 10^9 + 7. The maximum min-product value, before applying the modulo operation, will fit within a 64-bit signed integer.
constraints: The min-product of a nonempty contiguous subarray is its minimum times its sum.
Return the maximum min-product modulo 1,000,000,007 after maximizing the unmodded value.
hints: For each value, find the widest subarray where it is a minimum.
A monotonic stack discovers that span when a smaller or equal value arrives.
Use prefix sums to obtain each popped span sum in constant time.
Every subarray’s minimum is popped once with its maximal valid span; positivity means that widest span maximizes the sum for that minimum.
editorial: Every subarray’s minimum is popped once with its maximal valid span; positivity means that widest span maximizes the sum for that minimum.

tests.explanation: Subarray [2,3,2] has minimum two and sum seven, producing fourteen.
Subarray [2,3,3] has minimum two and sum eight, producing sixteen.
